_note: Maps interactive_id tags (Blender custom properties -> glTF node extras -> three.js object.userData) to website behaviour. Kept separate from model generation. kind: navigation = leads to a site section (always ALSO reachable through normal HTML links); discovery = optional reward, never needed to navigate. scope = which exhibit listens (home = desk homepage, games = Games page, about = About page). A click on any child mesh resolves to the nearest ancestor with an interactive_id. Routes are internal paths; external links (href) are only ones the existing site already uses (see AUDIT.md). Panel copy is taken from the existing site ('source').

panel.title: Choose your next world.
panel.text: Start here: choose a cartridge, hear it click into place, and see where the project stands. Explore the project pages for development updates and a closer look at each world.

panel.title: About the Studio
panel.text: Brok3n by Design is an independent game studio where each project is designed, directed, and built by a single creator using modern creative tools. The studio brings together strange ideas, dark humor, nostalgia, and experimental mechanics. Every project explores something a little different — from retro RPGs and satirical personality tests to haunted card games and fictional radio stations.

panel.text: A shared pixel-art guestbook where every visitor can draw, sign, and leave a permanent mark on the wall.

panel.title: Studio Passport
panel.text: Collect a stamp for every corner of the studio you find: the project pages, the hidden things, the odd ones out. Your stamps stay in this browser.

panel.title: Projects in the works
panel.text: The pile of folders where the unfinished ideas live: The Maze, Macabre Dolls and Juicebox, and whatever turns up next. Sketches, notes, test scenes. Nothing in here is a promise yet.

panel.title: The detention mug
panel.text: “We're all pretty bizarre. Some of us are just better at hiding it, that's all.” — The Breakfast Club (1985). Still warm. Somebody is coming right back.

panel.title: My Gaming History
panel.text: The games I grew up with, the ones that stuck with me, and why I still love gaming today: point-and-click adventures, decades of shooters, and building systems that run themselves.

panel.title: Collectible
panel.text: Raising a tiny mug to everyone still shipping at this hour.

panel.title: Bookworm
panel.text: A shelf of well-thumbed reference books. One of them is suspiciously well-worn.

panel.title: The bug emergency kit
panel.text: Break glass in case of bugs. Inside: one rubber duck, for explaining the problem to. Around it: backup ducks, because some bugs need a committee.

panel.title: Finds from Bid & Buried
panel.text: Some of what turned up in the storage units, still in pixels: Dusty Explorer's Globe, the green banker's lamp, a red toolbox with the cash someone left on it, a trophy and a few coins.

panel.title: Occupied
panel.text: Somebody found the warm jumper. Somebody is not moving. Close it gently.

panel.title: Seven ducks
panel.text: Each one has heard a full explanation of a bug, out loud, and fixed it by listening. None of them can code. That's the point.

panel.title: Dusty Explorer's Globe
panel.text: Best find of day two: appraised at $142. The lamp is common, the toolbox is good, the trophy is somebody's whole childhood. Sell it, stash it or scrap it.

panel.title: The drawer cat
panel.text: Asleep on the good jumper since the last deadline. Purrs if you look. Will not be moving for the next build, or the one after that.

panel.title: Under the Radar
panel.text: Your next favourite is one you’ve never heard of. Follow your curiosity into a world of quiet surprises and unexpected connections. Some things are worth a closer look.

panel.title: Maker's plate
panel.text: Handmade by Brok3n by Design. No warranty, express or implied. Please stop looking under things.

panel.title: Rubber Duck Rental
panel.text: It listens. You debug. That's the deal. (A word from WRFM 97.1's sponsor.)

radio.idea: two buttons: tune in to WRFM 97.1 live (in sync with the real station, keeps playing on every page) or play a funny clip

panel.title: WRFM 97.1
panel.text: Tune in to the station live: the same song, at the same second, as everyone listening right now. It keeps playing while you look around the site. Or play one of the funny clips: callers, sponsors and Vera Lang herself.

panel.title: The Doubloon Club
panel.text: Five kids, one map, no grown-ups. The studio's favourite film that doesn't exist: summer, bikes, a skull-shaped rock and a ship in the fog. Made up from scratch, characters and all, as a love letter to the adventure films we grew up on.

panel.title: The club's treasure map
panel.text: Follow the dots from the beach, past the compass, to the X by Skull Cove. Gus drew it. Gus is not sure which way is north.

panel.title: You found the back
panel.text: Most people never turn the desk around. Behind every finished thing there's tape, a map and a poster for a film that only exists here.

panel.title: Sunglasses
panel.text: “Life moves pretty fast. If you don't stop and look around once in a while, you could miss it.” — Ferris Bueller's Day Off (1986).

panel.title: Made in Canada
panel.text: A little flag on the back of the monitor, where only the curious look. Brok3n by Design is made in Canada.
